title: Concord Heartbeat: SLO Activation Playbook & Cross-Functional Sprint
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact, operational playbook for running a 10-week cross-functional sprint (mini-initiative) to activate and validate SLOs across three product pillars: Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private. Outcome is not just a list of SLOs but: runnable runbooks, verified telemetry, capacity burn experiments, and a rollback/fallback matrix that product teams can adopt.

Scope (what we will do in this initiative):
- Define 2 core SLOs per pillar (availability and p95 latency) with clear measurement definitions.
- Create and publish a standard SLO runbook template and at least one completed runbook per pillar.
- Run chaos-ish capacity/latency experiments in staging and shadow in prod where safe.
- Wire alerts -> playbooks -> responder on-call (liaison role) and validate paging flows.
- Track quality metrics (user-facing errors, model-fallback frequency) and unit-cost impact for the rollouts.

Out-of-scope:
- Full org-wide SLA contracts (legal/pricing)
- Re-architecting runtime kernels — we will use config-level controls and routing policies only.

Primary goals (success criteria):
- Each product pillar has a published SLO doc with: measurement query, burn rate calculation, alert thresholds, action runbook.
- Two tabletop exercises and one live simulated degradation per pillar completed with <10% missed actions in the runbook checklist.
- Observability gaps reduced: at least 3 missing signals identified and onboarded into dashboards.
- A cost-vs-quality note per pillar with recommendations (e.g., batching tweaks, quantization swap, or routing fallbacks).

Stakeholders & Roles:
- Initiative Lead: Sofia Martinez (SRE) — overall coordination, reporting to eng leadership.
- Product Pillar Leads: Daniel Kim (Hosted API), Priya Natarajan (Dedicated), Liam O'Connor (Private).
- Platform Partner: Rae Chen (Platform Eng) — telemetry & infra changes.
- Applied ML: review model-fallback behavior and help define acceptable quality degradation.
- Solutions Eng / CS: assess downstream customer impact for simulated experiments.
- Oncall Liaisons: one named oncall per pillar for the exercise weeks.

Working cadence and communication:
- Weekly 45m sync: Tuesdays 10:00am PT. Rolling notes in Confluence page (linked in metadata).
- Fast channel: #concord-heartbeat (Slack) for alerts, test updates, and postmortems.
- Milestone demos: end of week 5 (midpoint) and week 10 (wrap).

High-level timeline (10 weeks):
- Week 0 (prep): finalize SLO definitions, measurement queries, and runbook template.
- Weeks 1-3 (instrument): ensure metrics exist for all SLOs, build dashboards, create alert rules in staging.
- Weeks 4-5 (tabletop + refine): run tabletop exercises; iterate on runbooks; fill missing telemetry.
- Weeks 6-7 (staging stress tests): capacity/latency tests in staging; track burn rates and alert fidelity.
- Week 8 (canary shadow in prod): low-impact shadowing of failures with customer-simulated load; monitor.
- Week 9 (live experiment): run a guarded degradation experiment (preapproved rollback plan).
- Week 10 (wrap & handoff): consolidate runbooks; create 30/60/90 day followup tasks; exec summary.

Milestones with owners and acceptance:
- SLO Definition Complete (owner: Pillar Leads) — acceptance: measurement query returns expected baseline and historical computation validated.
- Runbook Template Published (owner: SRE lead) — acceptance: template reviewed by product and platform.
- Telemetry Gaps Closed (owner: Platform Partner) — acceptance: dashboards show all SLO signals for last 30 days.
- Tabletop Completed (owner: Pillar Leads + Oncall Liaison) — acceptance: all runbook steps exercised in dry-run and noted actions created.
- Live Experiment Executed (owner: Initiative Lead) — acceptance: rollback executed cleanly if thresholds exceeded; postmortem within 48 hours.

Operational checklists (short):
- Before any live experiment: stakeholder signoff, paging list verified, automated rollback scripts smoke-tested, customer-impact guardrails confirmed.
- Alerting hygiene: alerts must be actionable and documented in runbook (no alert storms).
- Oncall readiness: liaison has 1:1 with primary oncall, knows escalation path.

Risk & mitigations (top 4):
- Customer-visible degradation: mitigate with low-impact shadow runs, gradual ramp and immediate fallback to lower-capacity model variant.
- Missing telemetry causing false positives/negatives: hold a telemetry sprint in weeks 1-3 and require instrumentation tickets to be resolvable within 5 days.
- Pager fatigue / noise: enforce a pre-runbook filter and set burn-rate alerts conservatively in staging.
- Capacity overruns during staging: use quota caps and autoscaling test knobs to control blast radius.

Metrics to track (minimum):
- SLO-specific: p95 latency, availability percent, error-rate (4xx/5xx) per route.
- Operational: Mean Time To Acknowledge (MTTA), Mean Time To Mitigate (MTTM), number of runbook steps completed.
- Business: a synthetic user success-rate, and model-fallback frequency.
- Cost: delta in token-cost / inference-second during experiments.

Runbook template (brief outline):
- Title, SLO reference, measurement query, alert thresholds, initial triage checklist (what to look for), quick mitigations (disable feature, route to fallback), escalation ladder, rollback steps, postmortem checklist.

Acceptance & handoff:
- At wrap: handoff doc bundle (SLO doc, runbook, dashboards, experiment logs, postmortem) added to the product pillar repo + Confluence.
- Each pillar to schedule a 30-day followup to verify adoption and surface any behavioral regressions.

Experiment examples (practical ideas):
- Latency injection: add synthetic delay on model calls inside staging mesh and validate p95 alert triggers and fallback routing.
- KV cache cold-start: flush local KV caches to simulate cold traffic and observe latency profile and cache-warmup patterns.
- Autoscaling treadmill: throttle GPU pool scaling to observe queue growth and admission control responses.

Deliverables (expected artifacts):
- canonical SLO doc per pillar (markdown)
- SLO runbook per pillar (markdown + checklist)
- dashboards and alert rules in observability platform
- experiment logs and analysis note (cost/impact)
- postmortem and improvement backlog items

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Who signs off for live experiment beyond product and SRE? (Security/Trust?)
- Need legal check for any simulated customer-impact tests (esp. for Private deployments).
- Confirm quota knobs for Dedicated clusters with infra for week 6.
- Identify a safe time-window for shadowing in prod for each region.

Next steps (this week):
1) Publish this playbook as draft and invite pillar leads for inline edits (owner: Sofia).
2) Create measurement-ticket templates and assign to pillar leads (owner: Platform Partner).
3) Schedule week0 prep meeting and tabletop calendar.

Appendix: quick links and snippets
- Suggested burn-rate alert formula: burn_rate = errors_now / (error_budget_rate * window) — keep conservative multiplier in first run.
- Minimal runbook step example: 1) confirm alert scope 2) check model-fallback metrics 3) trigger routing-fallback if p95 > threshold for 2 consecutive windows 4) notify #concord-heartbeat 5) escalate to oncall liaison.

Signed-off-by: Sofia Martinez (SRE) — draft for review.
